clue.text: Capable of producing iron French roofing material

parts.note: fer is the French word for the metal iron
a tile is a slab of baked clay used to cover roofs

explanation.surface: A description of some French ironwork that turns out to make roof covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron French' is one piece: the French word for iron, not the chemical symbol FE plus a separate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertile land or animals can bear crops or young, that is, they are productive.

clue.text: Alien and heretofore ignoble in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stranger who has been base up to now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' points to the run inside heretoFORE IGNoble.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien and foreign both describe what comes from another country or is strange.

clue.text: Right libel one shamefully in revolution

indicators.note: shamefully suggests letters treated badly, knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone shamefully defamed during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shamefully' rearranges LIBELONE to EBELLION.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion is an uprising against authority, a revolution.

clue.text: I had to go to Douglas's place to find peculiarity of speech

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: A traveller visiting Douglas to learn a local turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas looks like a person but is the capital of the Isle of Man (IOM).
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression or usage peculiar to a language.

clue.text: Endlessly wealthy after city money case?

indicators.note: after says the trimmed word follows the rest

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a cent is a coin, money

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A rich person in the City handling a money case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts RICH to RIC. EC is the postal district of the City of London. 'case' is an odd person, not a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a case means they are an odd character, an oddball.

clue.text: Popular drink I had proved tasteless

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sip is a small drink
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a fashionable drink turned out to be bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food lacks flavour; the word is a plain synonym of bland.

clue.text: Committed deadly sin as primitive instincts came first

parts.note: the id is Freud's term for the primitive instincts
led means came first, was in front

explanation.surface: A sinner whose base urges took over.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloth, or idleness, is one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is a deadly sin, so being lazy or doing nothing commits it.

clue.text: Health resorts with blazing fires serving simple characters

parts.note: a san, short for sanatorium, is a health resort

indicators.note: blazing suggests letters flying about in a fire, rearranged

explanation.surface: Spa hotels with roaring fires and plain fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blazing' rearranges FIRES to SERIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Typefaces without serifs, the small strokes at letter ends, are plain letter forms.

clue.text: Scheme to catch one is without elegance

indicators.note: to catch means the word holds another inside

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A scheme to trap someone that lacks finesse.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple, unadorned, lacking refinement.

clue.text: Light coat for housework?

explanation.surface: A question whether a thin layer is the cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer of powder or sugar is a light covering; wiping away dirt with a cloth is a household chore.

clue.text: Teacher's not quite an inexperienced type

indicators.note: not quite says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a rabbit is slang for a poor or novice player, especially in cricket or tennis

explanation.surface: A remark that some teacher is still a bit green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter T from RABBIT. A rabbit is British sporting slang for a weak, inexperienced player.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and scholar.

clue.text: Lends a car out for many months here?

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A car-hire firm lending out a vehicle for many months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LENDSACAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendars set out the days of every month of a year, so many months appear on them.

clue.text: Doomed poorly old people supported by editor

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece supported by another has it following

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ill
men is a word for people in general

explanation.surface: A gloomy picture of sick elderly folk propped up by an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' puts ED after ILLOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-omened is ill-fated, attended by bad signs.

clue.text: Wickedness on road to where commandments were given?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: sin is wickedness
the A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, written with the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Sin on the road to the mountain where Moses got the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is where, in the Bible, Moses received the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Scotsman returned advertisement for nymph

indicators.note: returned says the name is turned back to front

parts.note: Ian is the stock Scottish man's name in crosswords
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A Scotsman sending back an advert about a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IAN into NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a naiad is a water nymph of rivers and springs.

clue.text: Was a long time with daughter brought up as a madcap

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lived means was, existed
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A reckless child, brought up long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns LIVEDERAD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless person, a madcap.

clue.text: Looking about

explanation.surface: A plain two-word phrase about searching around.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at, so the participle means looking; as a preposition it means concerning, on the subject of.

clue.text: One fights potential arguer about evil

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round another word
potential suggests what the letters could become, rearranged

parts.note: ill can mean evil, harm

explanation.surface: A fighter who would argue about wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges ARGUER to GUERRA, which goes 'about' ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular fighter in a small armed band.

clue.text: Liberal abandoned restraint in copy

indicators.note: abandoned says the party is dropped from the word

parts.note: a limitation is a restraint

explanation.surface: A political note about a party throwing off its restraints.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a copy, a replica.

clue.text: In clever changes takes time to be a bit brainy?

indicators.note: takes means the rearranged letters take in another letter
changes means the letters are altered in order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clever who keeps changing their mind, taking time over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges INCLEVER to VENRICLE, which 'takes' T inside. The definition is a pun: a bit of the brain, not slightly brainy.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain contains four ventricles, fluid-filled cavities, so one is part of that organ.

clue.text: Woman circles mountain to find a fragrant plant

indicators.note: circles means the name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
ben is a Scottish word for mountain

explanation.surface: A hill walker circling a peak in search of a scented flower.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden plant, and lemon verbena is grown for its scent.

clue.text: Needing to lose weight to keep measurement slight

indicators.note: to keep means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: someone fat needs to lose weight
IN is the abbreviation for inch, a measurement

explanation.surface: A dieter told to lose weight while keeping their measurements small.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint chance or resemblance is slight, barely there.

clue.text: Article on an old actor mostly appearing here?

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: An article about an old actor and where he performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TREE to TRE. Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the building where actors perform on stage.

clue.text: Mad attempt to follow artist

indicators.note: to follow says the attempt comes after the artist

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist
a bid is an attempt

explanation.surface: A crazed attempt to copy a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means fanatical or furious, like a crazed animal.

clue.text: Squanders money to get a piece of music

explanation.surface: Someone who wastes their cash, and the song that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is old British slang for spending it recklessly; a blues is a melancholy song.

clue.text: Salt's concern about a number in ship

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the rest

parts.note: care is concern

indicators.note: in puts the number inside the ship

parts.note: a boat is a ship

explanation.surface: Concern for a sailor about a number of people on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a sailor, and 'concern' like a worry about the crew, but the salt is chemical; 'in' and 'about' nest the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbonate is a chemical salt of carbonic acid, such as chalk.

clue.text: Timeless distinguishing mark of something hidden

indicators.note: timeless says the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: a cachet is a distinguishing mark or seal

explanation.surface: A timeless mark of something secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' drops T, the abbreviation for time, from CACHET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or weapons.

clue.text: On active service on island finds calm amid turbulence

parts.note: OAS is the military abbreviation for on active service

explanation.surface: A soldier on an island finding peace in the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is figuratively a peaceful refuge in a troubled setting, like a fertile spot in a desert.

clue.text: Suspect's similarly loud?

parts.note: equi- is the Latin-derived prefix meaning equal or alike
vocal means outspoken, loud

explanation.surface: Someone suspicious who is just as noisy as the others.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair as equivocal evidence is doubtful; the wordplay splits the word into a Latin prefix for equal and a word for loud, as if it meant speaking with equal voices.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivocal evidence is ambiguous, so it is open to doubt or questionable.

clue.text: Examine evidence about Henry's move

indicators.note: about means the word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sift is to examine evidence closely
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A detective examining evidence about a man called Henry and his next move.
explanation.walkthrough: The henry is the SI unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a change of position, a move.

clue.text: Forgive a bachelor's misplaced love

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters of the word are set in the wrong places

explanation.surface: Forgiving a single man whose love went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges LOVE to OLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to pardon them, freeing them from blame.

clue.text: One cherishes British nurse's recipe for increasing fondness?

indicators.note: cherishes is read as holds close, so one word embraces the others

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice
SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A British nurse with a fond patient, read as a recipe for affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cherishes' embraces the British nurse inside the card. The definition refers to the proverb about the heart growing fonder. SEN was an old British nursing qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says time apart makes the heart grow fonder, so being away is the formula for more love.
